commits.edited_message:
set alpha_dithering in VP8InitDithering

VP8InitDithering runs before the alpha plane is decoded and before
the alpha pre-processing level is even known, so deferring the
ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS check to VP8DecompressAlphaRows reads the
same header byte a second time for no benefit.

Initialize dec->alpha_dithering once, from the decoding options,
and only decode all alpha rows in one pass in VP8DecompressAlphaRows
when dec->alpha_dithering > 0.

Change-Id: I723363f8ac482cd2419c585c68f6fb468a54926d

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c), except for streams using
ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS, which WebPDequantizeLevels() needs in
full when alpha dithering is active.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a heap-buffer-overflow write in the lossy+alpha decode path
(VP8LColorIndexInverseTransformAlpha via DecodeAlphaData -> ExtractPalettedAlphaRows)
and only emerges when BOTH edited commits are read together:

Commit 0853442 (earlier) removes the ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS gate that
VP8InitDithering() previously applied when initializing dec->alpha_dithering.
On its own it is harmless: dec->alpha_dithering is now set straight from the
user's alpha_dithering_strength option, and the single-pass full-image alpha
decode in VP8DecompressAlphaRows (keyed on dec->alpha_dithering > 0) is still
backed by a full-height alpha plane, because at this point AllocateMemory()
unconditionally allocates width*height rows for dec->alpha_plane.

Commit c6ad323 (later) shrinks dec->alpha_plane to a small sliding window
(~106 rows for a 320-row image) in AllocateMemory(), but gates the full-height
allocation on exactly the property commit 0853442 stopped maintaining: it
allocates the full plane only when the alpha header advertises
ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS, on the premise that dec->alpha_dithering > 0 implies
that property (the premise the original 0853442 guaranteed). On its own (with
the original 0853442 in place) it is also harmless: dec->alpha_dithering > 0
still implies level pre-processing.

Composed, the premise breaks: a plain lossless-compressed alpha stream
(pre_processing != ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS, e.g. a fine alpha gradient
produced by the public encoder) decoded with the documented
WebPDecoderOptions.alpha_dithering_strength > 0 now (a) sets
dec->alpha_dithering > 0, which makes VP8DecompressAlphaRows decode the whole
image in one pass (num_rows = height - row), while (b) WebPGetAlphaWindowRows
allocates only ~106 rows of alpha. The full-image decode then writes far past
the end of the sliding window allocation.

A correct fix is non-local: reverting the frame_dec.c hunk of either commit
alone leaves an inconsistent state.
 - Fixing only commit 0853442's diff (restoring the pre-processing gate in
   VP8InitDithering) is sufficient, but that gate lives in a different commit
   and file than the allocation whose safety depends on it; a reviewer who
   only repairs the allocation side (commit c6ad323) by keying
   WebPGetAlphaWindowRows on dec->alpha_dithering again still leaves the
   one-pass full-image decode keyed on the now-ungated option, and vice versa.
 - Fixing only commit c6ad323's diff (e.g. re-keying the full-height allocation
   on dec->alpha_dithering) does not restore the invariant 'the single-pass
   decode only happens for level-preprocessed streams', it only re-couples one
   of the two sites; the two conditions must be made consistent across both
   commits (or the single-pass decode re-gated on the actual allocation size),
   which requires reasoning across both diffs.
Verified: probe fires (ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE, rc 134/SIGABRT) only on
the tree with both edits; with either single edit applied over the original
batch the probe decodes cleanly (rc 0), and the original batch is clean.

pocs.entry_point: WebPEncodeRGBA (webp/encode.h) to produce the in-contract lossy+alpha WebP bytes, then WebPDecode (webp/decode.h) with WebPDecoderOptions.alpha_dithering_strength = 100
